name: Chronix
tagline: Time-series store on Apache Solr that packed compressed chunks of points into documents; archived since 2019.
description: Chronix was an open-source time-series database from the German consultancy QAware that layered on Apache Solr and Lucene instead of implementing its own storage engine. It grouped consecutive data points into compressed chunks stored as Solr documents alongside descriptive attributes, so long histories of operational metrics took little space and could be filtered with ordinary Solr queries plus Chronix functions for aggregations and analyses; Spark and other integrations were separate modules. Development stopped after Chronix Server 0.5.2 in November 2019 and the main repository is archived. Its chunked-compression approach is now standard in engines such as Prometheus, VictoriaMetrics and QuestDB, which are the sensible choices today.
statusNote: Repository archived on GitHub; last release Chronix Server 0.5.2 (Nov 2019).
strengths: Chunked, compressed storage kept long metric histories small
Reused Solr/Lucene for indexing, replication and tooling
Attribute-rich series could be filtered with standard Solr queries
weaknesses: Small community with few integrations beyond the original team's
useCases: Historical reference for chunk-based time-series storage on a search engine
notIdealFor: Production workloads that need updates or support
